question: Consider a bivariate real array F(x,y) = q(u(x) + v(y)), where q is a real polynomial of degree at most d and u, v are arbitrary real-valued functions of the row index x and column index y respectively. Prove that F factorizes as a matrix product A * B with inner dimension d+1, and conclude that the rank of F is at most d+1. Make explicit which polynomial identity provides the factorization and why only the degree of q — not the number of rows or columns — controls the inner dimension.

source_refs.anchor: lines 23-50: FactorsThrough F := exists A : Matrix a i R, B : Matrix i b R, F = A*B; FactorsThrough.rank_le : F.rank <= Fintype.card i; polynomial_add_factorization (p) (d) (hd: p.natDegree <= d) (u v) : FactorsThrough (i := Fin (d+1)) (fun x y => p.eval (u x + v y)) via A x i = (taylor (u x) p).coeff i, B i y = v y^i; polynomial_add_rank_le : rank <= d+1
